transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I came in because I’ve been doing some things that don’t really make sense, especially at work and school. Like, I’ll line receipts across the floor, or tap the calculator in sets of nine. Sometimes I’ll just stand by the copier with my hands held up until someone asks if I’m okay. It’s starting to worry me.
Do you feel less anxious when you're doing things like lining up receipts or tapping the calculator?

Not really less anxious, no. It’s more like I just start doing it and then realize it looks strange. Like with the receipts or tapping the calculator in nines, it doesn’t feel like it helps much—it’s just something I end up doing.
Do you have thoughts that keep repeating in your mind and won't go away?
I don’t think so. I mean, I get thoughts stuck sometimes like anyone, but not really thoughts that repeat over and over and won’t go away. At least I haven’t noticed that.
Do you feel like you have to do these actions, like lining up receipts or tapping the calculator, or could you stop yourself if you wanted to?

I think I could stop if someone pointed it out, or if I really focused on it. It doesn’t feel like I have to do it in the way where I’m forced. It’s more that I catch myself doing these odd things, like the receipts or the calculator tapping, and then I realize it doesn’t make much sense.
Do you have any thoughts that you try to ignore or suppress?

Not really. I mean, I don’t think I have thoughts that I’m actively trying to push away or suppress. Sometimes I’ll ignore things if I’m busy, but nothing that feels like it keeps coming back and I have to fight it off.
Do you think something bad would happen if you didn't do these things, like lining up the receipts or tapping the calculator?

No, I don’t think something bad would happen exactly. It’s not like I’m doing it to prevent anything. I just find myself doing it, like lining receipts across the floor or tapping the calculator in sets of nine, and then afterward I realize it doesn’t really make sense. Sometimes I’ll even just stand by the copier with my hands up until someone asks if I’m okay.
Do you feel like the things you do, such as lining up receipts, need to be done in a specific way or look a certain way to feel right?

Not really like it has to look a certain way. It’s more that I’ll just start doing it, like laying the receipts out across the floor or tapping the calculator in nines, and it doesn’t really make sense afterward. I’m not thinking, “It has to be perfect,” it’s just… I’m doing these odd things and then I notice how strange it looks.
Do these behaviors, like lining up receipts or tapping the calculator, interfere with your daily life or cause you significant distress?

Yeah, it has started to interfere. I failed an important course module, and at work my ledgers have been coming back with serious errors. I’ve had to ask for help because I can’t reliably finish things that used to be routine for me. It’s frustrating, honestly.
Do you feel like there's a specific reason or thought behind why you're doing these actions, like lining up receipts or tapping the calculator?

Not really a clear reason, no. I came in because I’ve started doing things at work and school that just don’t make sense to me, like lining receipts across the floor, tapping the calculator in sets of nine, or standing by the copier with my hands held up until someone asks if I’m okay. I’m not thinking through why I’m doing it — it just kind of happens, and then I notice how odd it is.
Do you feel like these actions, such as lining up receipts or tapping the calculator, are connected to any thoughts or ideas that you have?

I don’t really think they’re connected to any clear thoughts or ideas. It’s more like I just find myself doing them — lining the receipts across the floor, tapping the calculator in nines, or standing by the copier with my hands up — and then afterward I realize it doesn’t make much sense.
Do you feel like doing these actions helps you in any way, even if it's not about reducing anxiety?

No, I don’t really feel like it helps me. It’s not like I get something out of it or feel better afterward. I just catch myself doing things that don’t make sense, like spreading receipts across the floor or tapping the calculator in nines, and then I’m kind of embarrassed or confused about why I did it.
Do you ever feel like you're doing these actions because you're trying to follow some sort of internal rule?

I don’t think it feels like an internal rule, no. It’s more that I just start doing these odd things, like putting receipts across the floor or tapping the calculator in sets of nine, and then I kind of realize afterward that it doesn’t make sense. It doesn’t feel like I’m following a rule on purpose.
Do you feel like you have to repeat these actions a certain number of times to feel like you've done them correctly?

Not really. With the calculator, it might be in sets of nine, but I don’t feel like I have to do it that many times to make it “right.” I just sort of start doing it, or I’ll line receipts across the floor, or stand by the copier with my hands up, and then someone says something or I notice how strange it looks.
Do you feel like the things you do, such as lining up receipts, are done to make things look symmetrical or orderly?

No, not really. It’s not like I’m trying to make them neat or symmetrical. I’ll just start lining the receipts across the floor, or tapping the calculator in nines, and it doesn’t really look orderly or have a purpose. It’s more like I catch myself doing something that doesn’t make sense.
Do you feel like doing these actions gives you a sense of being in control of something?

No, I don’t think it makes me feel in control. It’s more like I just realize I’m doing something weird, like the receipts on the floor or standing at the copier with my hands up, and then someone asks if I’m okay. It doesn’t feel useful or like I’m controlling anything.
Do you think your actions, such as lining up receipts, would be okay if they were not done perfectly?

I don’t really think about it being perfect or not. Like with the receipts, I’m not trying to get them exactly right. I just start doing it, and then I notice it doesn’t make sense, or someone asks if I’m okay. So it’s not like I’d feel bad if it wasn’t perfect.
Do you feel like there's something wrong if the things you do, like lining up receipts, aren't done in a very specific way?

I don’t think so. I’m not really focused on doing it a certain exact way. It’s more like I notice I’m doing it, and it seems odd, but I don’t feel like something bad or wrong happens if it’s not done right.
Do you think your life would be easier or less stressful if you didn't feel the need to do these actions?

Yeah, I think it would be easier in the sense that people wouldn’t stop and look at me or ask if I’m okay. Like at work, when I’m lining receipts across the floor or tapping the calculator over and over, it just makes things awkward and gets in the way. I don’t really feel a “need” exactly, but if I wasn’t doing those things, it’d probably be less stressful.
Do you feel like doing these actions is something you cannot help but do?

Yeah… kind of. I don’t plan it out, but once I start doing it, it feels like I just keep going. Like lining receipts across the floor or tapping the calculator in sets of nine — I know it doesn’t really make sense, but I don’t always stop myself until someone notices or asks if I’m okay.
Do you feel like you would experience significant distress if you were prevented from completing one of these actions, such as lining up receipts?

Not really significant distress, no. It’s more like I get stuck doing it and it looks strange, like with the receipts on the floor or tapping the calculator nine times. If someone stopped me, I might feel thrown off or embarrassed, but I don’t think I’d panic or feel like something terrible would happen.
